title: T.O. cops cleared in deadly 2018 Scarborough pub shootout
article: Toronto Police and SIU at the scene of a police involved shooting at a commercial plaza near Warden Ave. and Hymus Rd., north of St. Clair Ave., in Toronto, Ont. on Thursday June 7, 2018. The car is marked with what are believed to be bullet holes. (Ernest Doroszuk/Toronto Sun/Postmedia )

The province's police watchdog has cleared Toronto cops of wrongdoing in last summer's deadly shootout with a gunman at a Scarborough pub - an incident that came dangerously close to claiming the life of one of the officers involved.

Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has been investigating the police-involved shooting since Robert Morfitt was gunned down in his car in a parking lot behind the Muckish Irish Pub, near Warden and Eglinton Aves., shortly after midnight on June 7, 2018.
Trouble began that night when Morfitt - a man with a violent criminal history - became embroiled in a fight with another patron in the pub.
"Multiple witnesses, including an off-duty police officer, noticed the complainant (Morfitt) was in possession of a handgun," the SIU said in a statement Thursday.
Morfitt, 36, exited the pub via a back door, inviting the other patron to take their dispute outside.
Meanwhile, the off-duty cop called 911 to report a man at the pub had a gun.
Numerous Toronto Police officers arrived to find Morfitt in the driver's seat of a white Mercedes.
"The officers approached the vehicle, ordering commands for the complainant to get out of the car," the SIU said.
"The complainant ignored the commands and, when (one of the officers) opened the driver's side door, pulled out a handgun and shot (that officer) in the chest."
The SIU said the officer returned fire, pulling his trigger three times, but his handgun jammed.
The officer is "unsure" if Morfitt fired first or if he shot first "as a reaction to seeing a firearm pointed at him," the SIU said.
One round struck the officer just below his heart.
"He felt the impact of being struck by the bullet, stumbled backwards in shock and looked for blood," the SIU said.
"The bullet pierced his memo book and shattered the glass on the cellphone he kept in his chest pocket, but was stopped by his bulletproof vest."
A second officer also opened fire on Morfitt, "emptying an entire magazine" from their service firearm, the SIU said, explaining a third cop armed with a C8 rifle shot once but missed.
"The shooting happened very quickly, in a matter of seconds," the SIU said.
"Afterwards, the complainant was slumped over with his face in the passenger seat of the Mercedes."
"He still had a handgun underneath his torso," the SIU added.
Officers pulled Morfitt from the car and performed CPR but he did not survive. Six bullets were later removed from his body.
Tony Loparco, the SIU's director until he stepped down from the job last month, ultimately determined there are no reasonable grounds to lay criminal charges against any of the officers involved.
"It is clear that the complainant produced a firearm and shot (an officer)," Loparco said.
"Irrespective of who shot first, the complainant presented a grave risk to (that officer) when he pointed a firearm at him."

"As such, the officers shooting at the complainant to neutralize that threat falls clearly within the scope of force permitted by law. Thus, no charges will issue and the case will be closed," he said.
